title: Identify interference sources, coupling paths and victims
summary: Map noise sources, coupling paths and susceptible circuits before choosing an EMC mitigation. Changing the path can be as useful as changing the source.
verification: Compare noise and victim behavior before and after a controlled mitigation.
limitations: A plausible coupling path is a hypothesis until measured; this is not a compliance test.

title: Plan emissions and immunity checks separately
summary: Assess both disturbances a product generates and disturbances it must tolerate. Component EMC characterization does not establish assembled-product performance.
applies_to: MCU products with defined environments and operating modes.
required_inputs: Intended environment and applicable product requirements
verification: Record emissions and functional behavior under the agreed disturbance tests.
limitations: Choose current product standards separately; this MCU note supplies no universal product limits.

citations.locator: EMC definitions; EMC characterization of microcontrollers

title: Define recovery from supply disturbances
summary: Select supported brownout/reset behavior and recovery handling for supply disturbances. Verify the selected threshold against the MCU operating range.
applies_to: MCUs with documented brownout and reset facilities.
required_inputs: MCU voltage/frequency limits and reset options
verification: Disturb the supply under controlled conditions and observe reset cause, outputs and restart.
limitations: Reset behavior is device-specific and does not guarantee safe system behavior by itself.

citations.locator: MCU design strategy: Brownout reset (BOR); Programmable voltage detector (PVD)

title: Assess edge rate as well as clock frequency
summary: Use signal transition time when assessing high-frequency content. A low repetition rate can still have fast edges that excite unwanted coupling.
verification: Measure edge shape and timing at the receiver before accepting a slew-rate change.
limitations: Slower edges must still satisfy the interface; nominal clock frequency is insufficient.

title: Plan signal return paths through cables and connectors
summary: Include cable and connector return conductors in the current-path review. Off-board wiring can carry noise and enlarge radiating loops.
applies_to: Signals leaving a PCB through a harness or connector.
verification: Trace signal and return paths through the complete interconnect; compare cable-dependent emissions.
limitations: Do not assign shield bonding or ground connections without system context.

citations.locator: Sections 2.5.3-2.5.4, Ground Returns and Signals Leaving the PCB

title: Evaluate source termination for ringing
summary: For a suitable point-to-point line, evaluate a resistor near the driver to reduce reflections. Include driver impedance when selecting it.
applies_to: Digital lines for which source termination suits the topology.
required_inputs: Driver impedance, line impedance and receiver load
verification: Simulate or measure receiver settling and timing across component tolerances.
limitations: No universal resistor value; multidrop and bidirectional buses need separate analysis.

title: Check ferrite impedance under operating current
summary: Choose ferrites using impedance versus frequency and DC bias, alongside current and voltage-drop limits. A headline impedance alone can misrepresent filtering in operation.
applies_to: Ferrite beads used in power filtering.
verification: Evaluate attenuation and rail drop at operating current.
limitations: Current rating does not promise retained impedance; use the selected part data.

title: Check bead-capacitor resonance and damping
summary: A bead and low-loss capacitors can amplify noise near resonance. Evaluate damping with realistic parasitics and bias.
applies_to: Supply filters containing ferrites and capacitors.
required_inputs: Filter models, capacitor ESR and bias
verification: Check frequency response and load-step behavior for peaking.
limitations: Adding capacitance is not automatically an improvement; damping depends on the network.

title: Minimize the buck converter commutation loop
summary: Identify the changing current path between switch states. Keep the input bypass and switching-device connections compact to reduce parasitic inductance and radiated noise.
applies_to: Buck converter layouts; cited example is LMR160X0.
required_inputs: Input bypass placement and current paths
verification: Inspect the commutation loop geometry and measure switching transients.
limitations: Other converter topologies have different critical loops; follow the selected device layout.

title: Check converter input-filter interaction
summary: Size input filtering for the required conducted-noise attenuation and check its interaction with the converter. Resonant input impedance may require damping.
applies_to: Switching converters with added input filters; source demonstrates LMR160X0.
verification: Measure conducted noise and confirm stable startup and load transients.
limitations: Example component values and measured compliance margins do not transfer to another product.

title: Route incoming ESD through the protection connection
summary: Route an exposed line through the TVS connection before the protected circuit, avoiding a long shunt stub. Keep the discharge return inductance low.
applies_to: PCB lines using external ESD protection.
required_inputs: Discharge return and protected IC location
verification: Inspect connector-to-TVS-to-IC routing and the TVS return geometry.
limitations: Layout cannot compensate for unsuitable protection ratings or signal loading.

citations.locator: Section 2.1, Optimizing Impedance for Dissipating ESD, page 4

title: Separate exposed and protected routing
summary: Avoid routing exposed conductors alongside protected signals where an ESD pulse can couple around the protection path.
applies_to: Connector entry regions and protection circuits.
verification: Inspect adjacent layers as well as same-layer parallel routing.
limitations: No universal spacing is established here; validate the assembled product under the required stress.

citations.locator: Section 2.2, Limiting EMI from ESD, page 5
